title: internal/ethapi: eth_createAccessList applies state overrides without the active precompile set
body:
## Problem

`AccessList` applies state overrides with a `nil` precompile set and never installs a precompile set on the EVM it creates:

```go
// internal/ethapi/api.go:1356-1360 (master @ eedeb03aa)
if stateOverrides != nil {
	if err := stateOverrides.Apply(db, nil); err != nil {
		return nil, 0, nil, err
	}
}
```

Inside `override.Apply`, `p, isPrecompile := precompiles[addr]` on a nil map always yields `isPrecompile == false`. This produces two different failures:

1. **`code` on a precompile address is ignored without error.** The code is written to state, but the EVM created later uses the default precompile table, so the precompile still runs. With a ~100k-gas mock as `code` on `0x01`, `gasUsed` is 24512, versus 123583 for the same mock on an ordinary address. `eth_call` with the same override runs the mock.
2. **`movePrecompileToAddress` fails with an incorrect error.** Because no address is seen as a precompile, the request is rejected with `account 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000004 is not a precompile`, although `0x04` is the identity precompile. `eth_call` with the same override applies the move.

Reproduction for (2), geth v1.17.7 and master (eedeb03aa):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_createAccessList","params":[{"from":"0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266","to":"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001111","data":"0xdeadbeef"},"latest",{"0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266":{"balance":"0x21e19e0c9bab2400000"},"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000004":{"movePrecompileToAddress":"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001111"}}]}
```

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"account 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000004 is not a precompile"}}
```

The doc comment on `CreateAccessList` says state overrides "can be used to create the accessList while taking into account state changes from previous transactions", and `eth_call` / `debug_traceCall` / `eth_simulateV1` all apply precompile overrides, so `eth_createAccessList` is the outlier. The `nil` was introduced when state overrides were added to this method (#31497).

## Suggested fix

Build the active precompile set from the block's rules, pass it to `Apply`, and install it on each EVM the method creates, as `doCall` does. #34086 proposed this, with a test, but was closed by its author without a review:

```go
isPostMerge := header.Difficulty.Sign() == 0
rules := b.ChainConfig().Rules(header.Number, isPostMerge, header.Time)
precompiles := vm.ActivePrecompiledContracts(rules)
if stateOverrides != nil {
	if err := stateOverrides.Apply(db, precompiles); err != nil {
		return nil, 0, nil, err
	}
}
...
evm := b.GetEVM(ctx, statedb, header, &config, nil)
evm.SetPrecompiles(precompiles)
```

The precompile map is not modified during execution, so the same map can be reused across the access-list iterations.

## Possible follow-up (separate question)

`addressesToExclude` is built from `vm.ActivePrecompiles(rules)`, the canonical address list. After a move, the old address is still excluded and the new address is not, so the resulting access list may include the destination of a moved precompile. Whether moved precompiles should be excluded at their new address is a separate question.

## Related

#35228 fixes the same problem in `eth_estimateGas` (the precompile set is built and modified there, but never passed to the gas estimator's EVM).
author: reporter
